question: us-policy-positions:environment-energy.bottle-deposit
definition: yes = a state (or territorial) law requires a refundable deposit on beverage containers, in force 1/1/2026; no = no such deposit law in force (a repealed or not-yet-operative law counts as no, with a note). Every answer row carries preempts: true because a deposit system is a state-level program.
summarySource: State codes and agency pages fetched 9/28/2026 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, legis.iowa.gov, legislature.maine.gov, malegislature.gov, legislature.mi.gov, oregon.public.law, legislature.vermont.gov, delcode.delaware.gov, col.guamcourts.gov) plus CT DEEP, Hawaii DOH, NY DEC and Oregon OLCC pages; Wikipedia 'Container deposit legislation in the United States' and bottlebill.org (Guam page, Existing Programs list, © 2026) for context; no 2025 enactment of a new state deposit law was found.

US-CA.note: California sets a refund value of 5 cents under 24 fluid ounces and 10 cents at 24 fluid ounces or more; the program dates from the 1986 act.

US-CT.note: The deposit rose from 5 to 10 cents on 1/1/2024; the statute site cga.ct.gov could not be fetched, so the cite rests on the DEEP page and common citation.

US-HI.cite: Haw. Rev. Stat. ch. 342G, pt. VIII
US-HI.note: The Department of Health says the Deposit Beverage Container program has run since January 2005 under the 2002 law; the HRS site returned 403, so the chapter cite is unverified here.

US-IA.note: A refund value of 5 cents is paid by the consumer on each covered beverage container.

US-ME.note: The bottle law now sits in Title 38, chapter 33; the old Title 32, chapter 28 sections are repealed.

US-MA.note: The 1982 law covers carbonated beverages only; the 2014 ballot expansion failed.

US-MI.note: Initiated Law 1 of 1976 sets a 10-cent deposit.

US-NY.cite: N.Y. Envtl. Conserv. Law art. 27, tit. 10
US-NY.note: The Returnable Container Act requires a deposit of at least 5 cents; the nysenate.gov statute page returned 403.

US-OR.note: The refund value is 10 cents since 2017; canned wine was added on 7/1/2025 (OLCC page https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/pages/bottle_bill.aspx).

US-VT.note: A 2025 overhaul keeps the deposit and phases in a producer responsibility organization, with labeling changes on 7/1/2026 and PRO participation required from 7/1/2027 (DEC page https://dec.vermont.gov/waste-management/solid/product-stewardship/bottle-bill).

US-DE.cite: Del. Code Ann. tit. 7, § 6051 et seq. (77 Del. Laws c. 275)
US-DE.note: Delaware repealed its 5-cent deposit by SB 234 (2010), replacing it with universal recycling; deposits ended 12/1/2010 per the Wikipedia summary, and the current code carries no deposit requirement.

US-GU.note: The Guam Beverage Container Recycling Act of 2010 (P.L. 30-221) takes effect only after a written agreement with the Navy and Air Force commands, and no government page shows that happened; Guam EPA's 2026 Recycling Guide (https://epa.guam.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2026-Recycling-Guide.pdf) lists no redemption program.

US-AL.note: Weak: not on the Container Recycling Institute's complete 2026 list of U.S. deposit programs (10 states and Guam).
